result.question: Why did Zebul send messengers?

readings.answer: To inform Abimelech that Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers had come to Shechem and were stirring up the city against him.
readings.support: Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you

readings.answer: To tell Abimelech to come and lie in wait in the fields that night.
readings.support: Now then, tonight you and the people with you are to come and lie in wait in the fields

readings.answer: Because he was angry at Gaal’s words.
readings.support: heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, he burned with anger. | So he covertly sent messengers

assessments.reason: It matches the warning Zebul sends: “Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you,” which is precisely a warning to Abimelech about Gaal.

Zebul’s message also includes the instruction, “Now then, tonight you and the people with you are to come and lie in wait in the fields,” so stating his purpose as telling Abimelech to ambush is supported by the text even though the key focuses on the warning.
The sequence “he burned with anger. So he covertly sent messengers” supports anger at Gaal’s words as a causal reason for sending messengers, a different but text-based answer to “why.”

result.reason: Both a warning about Gaal and tactical instructions, as well as anger as a cause, are presented as reasons for sending messengers, so multiple materially different answers fit the question.
